title: Fourth-and-long late: the sticks, soft coverage and the sideline (and how Rice won with 6 seconds left)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. The backup source (football-film-room, branch "data") couldn't be read: "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session" (HTTP 403). So there's no new miss of yours to fix. It's a new concept tied to Thursday's Rice-Temple finish. It builds on Lesson 34 (the two-minute drill) and Lesson 38 (fourth down).

The big idea: late in a close game, the trailing team often faces 4th-and-long. It has to throw. Everyone knows it.So why does it work so often? Because the defense is scared of the long TD. It backs up and gives away the short middle.The offense only needs 10 yards. The defense is guarding 40.

White = offense, moving up. Yellow = defense. The dashed yellow line is the throw.

  1. A · The sticks. The first-down line, 10 yards ahead. On TV it's the yellow line.A catch one yard short is a turnover. A catch one yard past keeps the game alive.
  2. B · The soft zone. The defense drops 4 players deep and rushes only 3.Some coaches call this "prevent." It prevents the long TD. It doesn't prevent 15 yards.
  3. C · The throw past the sticks. The receiver runs just beyond the line, then turns.With only 3 rushers, the QB has time. He doesn't need a perfect throw, just one past the line.
  4. D · The sideline. A catch near the sideline lets the receiver step out. That stops the clock.In the middle of the field the clock keeps running, so the offense must spike the ball or use a timeout (Lesson 34).

Thursday's real example: Temple led Rice 27-17 with under 5 minutes left. ESPN gave Temple a 99.5% chance to win.Rice scored with 1:55 left: Gael Ochoa to Max Mosey, 9 yards. 27-24.Temple went three-and-out. Rice got the ball at its own 42 with 53 seconds left: 58 yards to go.On 4th-and-10, Patrick Crayton Jr. hit Jordan Clark for 18 yards. Past the sticks by 8.Then Crayton threw 30 yards to Jacurri Brown in the end zone. 6 seconds left. Rice 31, Temple 27.Rice also converted a 4th-and-10 earlier with a 47-yard catch by Mosey. Temple's coach said injuries had thinned his secondary.

Why it matters for bets: late scores swing spreads and totals. Rice's last 14 points turned a Temple cover into a Rice win.A team that trails by 3 to 10 late will throw on every down. Expect points, even in a slow game.That's why the board names "late garbage-time points" as a risk on Unders and team totals (Market 101, Lesson 57).

For your Film Room drill: it's the easiest call in football. Late, trailing, 4th-and-long: call pass.Check the clues anyway. Shotgun. 3 or 4 receivers. The defense brings in 6 defensive backs (dime, Lesson 2).Look at the safeties. If they start 20 yards deep, the defense is playing soft (Lesson 20).The one trap: a QB draw. When defenders drop deep, the middle opens for a run. It's rare on 4th-and-10, but it happens on 3rd-and-long.

Connecting the dots: Lesson 34 showed how the clock shapes a two-minute drive. Lesson 38 showed when teams go for it on 4th down. This lesson shows why 4th-and-10 isn't hopeless: the defense's fear of the big play gives up the small one.

Video: search YouTube for "Rice Temple 2026 highlights Jacurri Brown" and "prevent defense explained."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 6: Situations)

quiz.q: It's 4th-and-10 with 50 seconds left, and the offense trails by 3. What should you log in the Film Room drill?
quiz.w: Late, trailing, 4th-and-long: the offense has to throw. Shotgun and 3-4 receivers confirm it.

quiz.q: In the diagram, why does the defense line up 4 players deep (B)?
quiz.w: A soft zone guards against the big play. The cost is open space just past the sticks.

quiz.q: Why do receivers often catch late passes near the sideline (D)?
quiz.w: Out of bounds stops the clock, which saves a timeout or a spike.

quiz.q: On Rice's last drive, what did the 18-yard catch on 4th-and-10 do?
o: Got past the sticks and kept the drive alive
quiz.w: Jordan Clark's catch was 8 yards past the first-down line. Then Jacurri Brown caught the 30-yard TD with 6 seconds left.
